ut-fattoush: Tear the bread by hand into two-finger pieces and fry them in olive oil until browned.
Drain the bread on paper and dust it with half the sumac while it is still hot.
Cut the tomatoes, cucumbers and radishes into large uneven pieces; the salad should be rough rather than neat.
Tear the lettuce by hand and chop the herbs and spring onion.
Whisk a dressing from the lemon juice, pomegranate molasses, crushed garlic, the remaining sumac, oil and salt.
Toss the vegetables in the dressing, add the bread and serve at once.
ut-kibbeh-bil-sanieh: Soak the bulgur in cold water for twenty minutes and squeeze it completely dry.
Blitz the lean beef with one onion to a paste and work in the bulgur, salt and half the spices.
Knead the mass five minutes, wetting your hands, until it is smooth and tacky.
Fry the remaining onion, add the minced lamb, the spices and the pine nuts and cook ten minutes.
Press half the mass into an oiled tray in a one-centimetre layer, smoothing it with a wet palm.
Spread the filling and cover with the other half of the mass, smoothed the same way.
Cut it into diamonds down to the base, pour over the olive oil and bake at 200 °C for forty minutes, to a browned crust.
ut-kibbeh-bil-sanieh-gfnf: Soak the quinoa in cold water for twenty minutes and squeeze it completely dry.
Blitz the lean beef with one onion to a paste and work in the quinoa, salt and half the spices.
Knead the mass five minutes, wetting your hands, until it is smooth and tacky.
Fry the remaining onion, add the minced lamb, the spices and the sunflower seeds and cook ten minutes.
Press half the mass into an oiled tray in a one-centimetre layer, smoothing it with a wet palm.
Spread the filling and cover with the other half of the mass, smoothed the same way.
Cut it into diamonds down to the base, pour over the olive oil and bake at 200 °C for forty minutes, to a browned crust.
ut-shuwa: Grind the garlic, all the spices, the crushed dried limes, vinegar, oil and salt into a thick paste.
Cut deep slashes to the bone and rub the paste inside them and all over the outside.
Refrigerate overnight, twelve hours at least.
Wrap the meat in banana leaves, then tightly in two layers of foil. No gap may remain.
Set the parcel on a tray, pour a cup of water into the tray and bake at 130 °C for eight hours.
Unwrap it, pour off the juices and cook the rice in them. Pull the meat into threads by hand.
Serve the meat over the rice, from a shared platter, eaten by hand.
ut-omani-mishkak: Mix the tamarind, crushed garlic and ginger, all the spices, oil and salt into a marinade.
Cut the meat into one-and-a-half-centimetre cubes and coat it in the marinade.
Refrigerate for at least four hours, ideally overnight.
Thread the pieces onto skewers packed close, without gaps.
Get the coals hot — you should not be able to hold a palm above the grate for more than three seconds.
Grill a minute and a half on each of four sides, basting with the leftover marinade.
Slide the meat off the skewers into gluten-free flatbread, add raw onion and serve at once.
ut-ful-sudani: Drain the soaked beans, cover them with fresh water and boil ninety minutes, until completely soft.
Pour off most of the water, leaving half a cup, salt the beans and mash them about halfway.
Crush the garlic with salt and cumin and stir it through the beans.
Turn them into a wide bowl and pour the sesame oil over without stirring it in.
Scatter over the crumbled cheese, chopped tomato, onion, chilli and halved eggs.
Serve with lemon and gluten-free flatbread. It is eaten by hand from the shared bowl.
ut-asida-sudanese: Brown the meat with the onion and garlic, then add the tomato paste and coriander.
Add water, season and stew forty minutes, until the meat is tender.
Stir in the peanut butter and rain in the ground okra in a thin stream, stirring constantly.
Cook the sauce ten minutes; it turns thick and stringy.
Bring a litre of salted water to the boil, set a cup aside and rain in the gluten-free flour, working it with a stick.
Work it fifteen minutes, adding the reserved water, until the mass is dense and smooth.
Turn the asida onto a platter with a wet spoon, make a hollow and pour the mulah into it.
ut-asida-sudanese-nf: Brown the meat with the onion and garlic, then add the tomato paste and coriander.
Add water, season and stew forty minutes, until the meat is tender.
Stir in the sunflower seed butter and rain in the ground okra in a thin stream, stirring constantly.
Cook the sauce ten minutes; it turns thick and stringy.
Bring a litre of salted water to the boil, set a cup aside and rain in the gluten-free flour, working it with a stick.
Work it fifteen minutes, adding the reserved water, until the mass is dense and smooth.
Turn the asida onto a platter with a wet spoon, make a hollow and pour the mulah into it.
ut-zanzibar-pilau: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and soak it twenty minutes.
Simmer the beef with half the spices for forty minutes, until tender. Keep the broth.
Fry the onion in oil over medium heat for twenty minutes, to a deep brown, almost black.
Add the garlic, ginger and the remaining spices and warm them two minutes.
Add the cooked meat and the diced potato, stir and warm through five minutes.
Add the rice, pour in broth at one and a half times the volume of the rice, and season.
Bring it up, cover and cook twenty minutes on a low heat without lifting the lid. Rest it ten minutes.
ut-ndizi-nyama: Brown the beef, add the onion, garlic and ginger and fry until soft.
Add the tomatoes and curry powder and cook five minutes, until the tomatoes break down.
Add water level with the meat, season and stew thirty minutes, covered.
Peel the bananas under running water and cut them into thick rounds.
Add the bananas to the pot and cook twenty minutes, until tender.
Pour in the coconut milk and warm five minutes without letting it boil. Scatter with coriander.
ut-shorshe-ilish: Soak the mustard seeds in warm water for twenty minutes.
Grind them with two chillies, a pinch of salt and a little water into a smooth paste.
Rub the fish steaks with turmeric and salt and leave them ten minutes.
Heat the mustard oil until it smokes, take it off and let it cool a minute; raw mustard oil is acrid.
Add the nigella, pour in the mustard paste let down with half a cup of water, and cook three minutes.
Lay the fish in a single layer, add the remaining chillies whole, cover and stew twelve minutes.
Finish with a spoon of raw mustard oil, take it off the heat and serve with rice.
ut-bhuna-khichuri: Dry-roast the moong dal for five minutes, to a nutty smell, and rinse it.
Rinse the rice and dry it. Wet rice will not toast; it steams in its own water.
Heat the ghee, brown the potatoes and lift them out.
In the same ghee fry the bay, cinnamon and cardamom, then the onion and ginger until golden.
Add the rice and dal with the turmeric and cumin and toast them five minutes, stirring.
Add boiling water at twice the volume of the grain, return the potatoes, season and add the whole chillies.
Cover and cook twenty minutes on a low heat, then let it stand ten minutes without opening it.
ut-larb-lao: Toast the raw sticky rice in a dry pan for ten minutes, to a deep gold, stirring.
Grind the cooled rice in a mortar or mill to a coarse powder.
Chop the pork fine with a knife, but not to a paste; the pieces should stay distinguishable.
Cook the meat in a pan with two spoons of water over medium heat for five minutes, breaking up lumps.
Take it off the heat and let it cool to warm, about five minutes.
Stir in the fish sauce, lime juice, chilli, shallot and rice powder.
Add the herbs, toss and serve with sticky rice and raw vegetables.
ut-tam-mak-hoong: Peel the papaya and shred it into long fine strips with a knife or a som tam grater.
Pound the garlic and chillies in the mortar into a coarse paste.
Add the cut beans and bruise them lightly with the pestle.
Add the tomatoes and crush them until their juice runs.
Add the padaek, lime juice and palm sugar and mix with the pestle and a spoon.
Add the papaya and work the pestle, turning with the spoon, for two minutes, until the fibres soften.
Taste and adjust for sourness, salt and heat. Serve with sticky rice.
ut-souvla: Cut the meat into large pieces of about two hundred grams, keeping the fat; it is needed.
Salt and pepper them generously all over and leave them half an hour at room temperature.
Light the coals and rake them to the sides, leaving the centre clear. Direct heat under the meat is not wanted.
Thread the pieces onto the spit, leaving a centimetre between them.
Turn the spit slowly and continuously for two hours. The meat should darken gradually rather than crust at once.
Dust with oregano ten minutes before the end and squeeze lemon over.
Take it off, cut it coarsely and serve in pita with onion, tomato and parsley.
ut-halloumi-grilled: Soak the halloumi in cold water for fifteen minutes, drain it and pat it completely dry.
Cut the cheese into centimetre slices — thinner and it dries out, thicker and it will not heat through.
Cut the chilled watermelon into large cubes and keep it in the fridge until serving.
Heat a dry pan hard and sear the halloumi two minutes a side, to dark stripes.
Whisk the olive oil with the lemon juice, honey and pepper.
Arrange the watermelon, rocket and hot cheese, spoon over the dressing and scatter with mint. Serve at once.
ut-maltese-rabbit-stew: Cover the jointed rabbit with the wine, half the garlic and the bay leaves and refrigerate for a day.
Lift out the meat, dry it and brown it in olive oil. Keep the marinade.
Fry the onion and remaining garlic until soft, add the tomato paste and cook three minutes.
Return the meat, pour in the marinade, season and stew covered for an hour on a low heat.
Add the potato and carrot and stew twenty-five minutes more.
Add the peas for the last ten minutes.
Ladle off some of the sauce and dress gluten-free spaghetti with it as a first course. The meat follows.
ut-pastizzi: Knead a dough from the flour, water and salt, work it ten minutes and rest it half an hour.
Boil the split peas with the onion for forty minutes until completely soft, mash them and season.
Mix the ricotta with the eggs, parsley, salt and pepper.
Roll the dough very thin, spread it with fat, roll it up and chill it twenty minutes.
Cut the roll into pieces and flatten each into a round; the layers give the flakiness.
Add the filling and seal them: ricotta as an open-topped boat, peas as a closed diamond.
Bake at 220 °C for thirty minutes, to a deep gold, and serve hot.
ut-pastizzi-gf: Knead a dough from the gluten-free flour, water and salt, work it ten minutes and rest it half an hour.
Boil the split peas with the onion for forty minutes until completely soft, mash them and season.
Mix the ricotta with the eggs, parsley, salt and pepper.
Roll the dough very thin, spread it with fat, roll it up and chill it twenty minutes.
Cut the roll into pieces and flatten each into a round; the layers give the flakiness.
Add the filling and seal them: ricotta as an open-topped boat, peas as a closed diamond.
Bake at 220 °C for thirty minutes, to a deep gold, and serve hot.
ut-chivito: Pound the beef under film to four millimetres and season it.
Fry the bacon crisp and drain it on paper.
Get the pan very hot and sear the steaks forty-five seconds a side.
Lay the cheese on the meat in the pan and cover it for thirty seconds so it softens.
Fry the eggs with runny yolks and toast the cut buns in a dry pan.
Spread mayonnaise on both halves and layer lettuce, tomato, the steak with its cheese, ham, bacon and the egg.
Close it, spear it with a cocktail stick and an olive, and serve with chips.
ut-milanesa-a-la-napolitana: Pound the meat to five millimetres and season it.
Beat the eggs with crushed garlic and chopped parsley; that garlic in the egg wash is the Uruguayan touch.
Dip the pieces in the egg, then press them firmly into the breadcrumbs.
Let the coating set for fifteen minutes in the fridge.
Fry in hot oil three minutes a side, to a golden crust, and drain on a rack.
Lay the milanesas on a tray, spoon on the tomato sauce, cover with ham and cheese and dust with oregano.
Grill for four minutes, until the cheese melts and colours.
ut-milanesa-a-la-napolitana-gf: Pound the meat to five millimetres and season it.
Beat the eggs with crushed garlic and chopped parsley; that garlic in the egg wash is the Uruguayan touch.
Dip the pieces in the egg, then press them firmly into the gluten-free breadcrumbs.
Let the coating set for fifteen minutes in the fridge.
Fry in hot oil three minutes a side, to a golden crust, and drain on a rack.
Lay the milanesas on a tray, spoon on the tomato sauce, cover with ham and cheese and dust with oregano.
Grill for four minutes, until the cheese melts and colours.
ut-pepian: Simmer the chicken with an onion and salt for forty minutes. Keep the broth.
Toast the pumpkin and sesame seeds in a dry pan to a deep gold, stirring.
In the same pan char the chillies, tomatoes, tomatillos and garlic until blackened in patches.
Blend everything with two ladles of the broth and the cinnamon to a smooth sauce.
Pass the sauce through a sieve; the chilli skins left behind would spoil the texture.
Cook the sauce twenty minutes, stirring, until it thickens and darkens.
Add the chicken, potato and beans and stew fifteen minutes. Serve with rice and coriander.
ut-tamales-guatemaltecos: Simmer the pork with the onion and salt for an hour. Strain and keep the broth.
Toast the seeds, sesame, chillies and tomatoes in a dry pan and blend them with broth; that is the recado.
Cook the recado twenty minutes to thicken it and season.
Slake the masa harina with warm broth, add the melted lard and work it twenty minutes over a low heat.
Pass the banana leaves over a flame for ten seconds each so they turn pliable.
On a leaf spread the dough, then a piece of meat, a spoon of recado, a strip of pepper and an olive. Wrap in two leaves.
Stack the parcels seam down in a pot and steam them for an hour and a half.
ut-sancocho-dominicano: Marinate all the meats in lime juice, crushed garlic, oregano, salt and pepper for an hour.
Brown the meats in batches in a large pot.
Add the onion and pepper, cover with three litres of water and simmer an hour.
Add the cassava and yautía in large pieces and cook twenty minutes.
Add the sweet potato, plantain and corn and cook twenty minutes more.
Mash a couple of pieces of cassava in the pot so the soup thickens.
Stir in the coriander, check the salt and serve with white rice and avocado.
ut-mangu: Peel the plantains under water, halve them and boil in salted water for twenty minutes, until soft.
Set aside a cup of the cooking water and cool it.
Pickle the sliced onion in vinegar with salt and leave it fifteen minutes.
Mash the hot plantain with butter, adding the cold water, to a smooth purée.
Fry slices of salami and cheese in a dry pan until browned.
Fry the eggs and build the plate: purée, the onion and its vinegar on top, salami, cheese and egg alongside.
ut-doubles: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in warm water, add the flour, turmeric and salt and knead a soft dough.
Let the dough rise somewhere warm for an hour, until doubled.
Boil the chickpeas with garlic for an hour, until completely soft.
Fry the onion, add the curry powder and cumin, warm them a minute and stir in the chickpeas with half their liquid.
Mash a third of the chickpeas in the pot and cook ten minutes to thicken the sauce.
Divide the dough into small balls, rest them twenty minutes and flatten them by hand into discs.
Fry the baras twenty seconds a side in hot oil; they must stay soft. Put the channa between two baras and serve with tamarind.
ut-callaloo: Wash the leaves, strip the tough stems and chop them coarsely.
Fry the onion and garlic in butter until soft.
Add the leaves, okra, pumpkin, thyme and the whole scotch bonnet, and cover with water two fingers above.
Simmer forty minutes covered. No less: raw taro leaves burn the mouth.
Remove the chilli and thyme, add the coconut milk and warm it five minutes without boiling.
Break the soup down with a swizzle stick or a masher to a thick but not perfectly smooth purée.
ut-tave-kosi: Rub the lamb with salt, pepper, garlic and oregano and roast it at 190 °C for forty minutes, dotted with butter.
Parboil the rice for seven minutes and drain it.
Melt the remaining butter, stir in the flour and cook two minutes to a nutty smell.
Whisk the yoghurt with the eggs and salt, add the flour mixture and beat until completely smooth.
Stir in the rice. It takes up some of the moisture and keeps the custard from splitting.
Arrange the meat and its juices in a dish and pour the yoghurt mixture over.
Bake at 180 °C for forty-five minutes, until the top colours and the centre still trembles slightly.
ut-tave-kosi-gf: Rub the lamb with salt, pepper, garlic and oregano and roast it at 190 °C for forty minutes, dotted with butter.
Parboil the rice for seven minutes and drain it.
Melt the remaining butter, stir in the gluten-free flour and cook two minutes to a nutty smell.
Whisk the yoghurt with the eggs and salt, add the gluten-free flour mixture and beat until completely smooth.
Stir in the rice. It takes up some of the moisture and keeps the custard from splitting.
Arrange the meat and its juices in a dish and pour the yoghurt mixture over.
Bake at 180 °C for forty-five minutes, until the top colours and the centre still trembles slightly.
ut-byrek-me-spinaq: Scald the spinach with boiling water, drain it and wring it out dry by hand.
Chop the spinach and mix it with the crumbled cheese, spring onion, dill and pepper. Salt cautiously; the cheese is salty.
Oil a tin and lay in three sheets of filo, brushing each one.
Spread a third of the filling, cover with two oiled sheets and repeat twice more.
Finish with three sheets on top, tuck the edges in and brush generously with oil.
Score it into squares down to the base with a sharp knife; cutting it after baking will not work.
Bake at 190 °C for forty-five minutes, to a deep golden crisp crust.
ut-placinta: Knead a soft dough from the flour, warm water, a spoon of oil and salt, and work it ten minutes.
Divide it into six balls, oil them generously and leave them under film for forty minutes.
Mash the cheese with the egg and dill. Grate the pumpkin and mix it with sugar for the second filling.
Stretch a ball by hand on an oiled table into a thin round, until it turns translucent.
Put the filling in the middle and fold the edges to the centre, into a parcel or a round.
Flatten it with your palm to a centimetre and a half.
Cook in a hot dry pan four minutes a side, to a mottled crust.
ut-placinta-gf: Knead a soft dough from the gluten-free flour, warm water, a spoon of oil and salt, and work it ten minutes.
Divide it into six balls, oil them generously and leave them under film for forty minutes.
Mash the cheese with the egg and dill. Grate the pumpkin and mix it with sugar for the second filling.
Stretch a ball by hand on an oiled table into a thin round, until it turns translucent.
Put the filling in the middle and fold the edges to the centre, into a parcel or a round.
Flatten it with your palm to a centimetre and a half.
Cook in a hot dry pan four minutes a side, to a mottled crust.
ut-zeama: Cover the chicken with three litres of cold water, bring it up and skim.
Simmer forty minutes on a low heat with a whole onion.
Knead a stiff dough from the flour and eggs, roll it thin, let it dry and cut it into fine noodles.
Lift out the chicken and joint it, and add the carrot, pepper and potato to the broth.
After fifteen minutes add the noodles and cook five minutes.
Boil the borș separately, strain it and pour it into the soup. Cook five minutes.
Return the meat, season and stir in the lovage and parsley. Let it stand ten minutes.
ut-judd-mat-gaardebounen: Soak the meat in cold water for four hours, changing the water twice.
Cover it with fresh water, bring it up, boil ten minutes and drain.
Cover it again, add the bay leaves and simmer an hour and twenty, until tender. Keep the broth.
Pod the beans, scald them for a minute and slip the skin off each one.
Render the bacon, fry the onion in its fat, stir in the flour and cook two minutes.
Add two ladles of the broth and the cream, then the savory and the beans, and stew ten minutes.
Cut the meat into thick slices and serve with the beans and boiled potatoes.
ut-judd-mat-gaardebounen-gf: Soak the meat in cold water for four hours, changing the water twice.
Cover it with fresh water, bring it up, boil ten minutes and drain.
Cover it again, add the bay leaves and simmer an hour and twenty, until tender. Keep the broth.
Pod the beans, scald them for a minute and slip the skin off each one.
Render the bacon, fry the onion in its fat, stir in the gluten-free flour and cook two minutes.
Add two ladles of the broth and the cream, then the savory and the beans, and stew ten minutes.
Cut the meat into thick slices and serve with the beans and boiled potatoes.
ut-gromperekichelcher: Grate the potatoes, onions and shallots coarsely into one bowl.
Wring the mixture out in a cloth, but not bone dry; a little moisture is needed.
Mix in the eggs, flour, chopped parsley, salt and pepper.
Heat the oil to 175 °C. Hotter, and the edges burn before the middle is hot.
Drop the mixture in by the spoonful, flattened to half a centimetre, and fry three minutes a side.
Drain on a rack, salt them and serve hot with apple sauce.
ut-gromperekichelcher-gf: Grate the potatoes, onions and shallots coarsely into one bowl.
Wring the mixture out in a cloth, but not bone dry; a little moisture is needed.
Mix in the eggs, gluten-free flour, chopped parsley, salt and pepper.
Heat the oil to 175 °C. Hotter, and the edges burn before the middle is hot.
Drop the mixture in by the spoonful, flattened to half a centimetre, and fry three minutes a side.
Drain on a rack, salt them and serve hot with apple sauce.
ut-dograma: Cover the mutton with cold water, bring it up and skim thoroughly.
Simmer two hours with the bay, until the meat comes away from the bone.
Lift out the meat, cool it and pull it into threads by hand, discarding bones and sinew.
Crumble the flatbread by hand into pieces the size of a fingernail. Do not cut it.
Slice the onion thin and work it with a pinch of salt so it softens.
Mix the bread, meat and onion dry in a large bowl, and season.
Divide between bowls and pour over the strained boiling broth immediately before serving.
ut-ichlekli: Knead a stiff unleavened dough from the flour, water and salt and rest it under a cloth for thirty minutes.
Dice the mutton and fat small with a knife, and chop the onion as fine as you can.
Mix the meat, fat, onion, cumin, salt and pepper. Add no water; the onion supplies the juice.
Divide the dough in two, roll the larger piece into a round and line an oiled tin, leaving an overhang.
Spread the filling evenly, cover with the second sheet and seal the edges in a firm rope.
Make a small steam hole in the centre, brush with butter and cover with foil.
Bake at 180 °C for an hour under the foil, then uncover and give it ten more minutes to colour.
ut-ichlekli-gf: Knead a stiff unleavened dough from the gluten-free flour, water and salt and rest it under a cloth for thirty minutes.
Dice the mutton and fat small with a knife, and chop the onion as fine as you can.
Mix the meat, fat, onion, cumin, salt and pepper. Add no water; the onion supplies the juice.
Divide the dough in two, roll the larger piece into a round and line an oiled tin, leaving an overhang.
Spread the filling evenly, cover with the second sheet and seal the edges in a firm rope.
Make a small steam hole in the centre, brush with butter and cover with foil.
Bake at 180 °C for an hour under the foil, then uncover and give it ten more minutes to colour.
ut-kabsa: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and soak it twenty minutes.
Fry the onion in ghee until golden, then add the garlic, cardamom and cinnamon.
Brown the chicken on all sides, then add the tomato paste, tomatoes, carrot and baharat.
Pierce the dried limes, drop them in, add water and simmer thirty minutes.
Lift out the chicken, pat it dry and put it under the grill for ten minutes, to a browned skin.
Add the rice to the broth at one and a half times its volume in liquid, season, and cook twenty minutes covered.
Fry the almonds and raisins in ghee, mound the rice on a platter, set the chicken on it and scatter the nuts over.
ut-kabsa-nf: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and soak it twenty minutes.
Fry the onion in ghee until golden, then add the garlic, cardamom and cinnamon.
Brown the chicken on all sides, then add the tomato paste, tomatoes, carrot and baharat.
Pierce the dried limes, drop them in, add water and simmer thirty minutes.
Lift out the chicken, pat it dry and put it under the grill for ten minutes, to a browned skin.
Add the rice to the broth at one and a half times its volume in liquid, season, and cook twenty minutes covered.
Fry the sunflower seeds and raisins in ghee, mound the rice on a platter, set the chicken on it and scatter the sunflower seeds over.
ut-jareesh: Soak the cracked wheat in cold water for two hours and rinse it.
Fry one onion in ghee, add the meat and brown it.
Add the tomatoes, baharat and pierced limes, cover with water and cook forty minutes.
Add the wheat, top up with water two fingers above and cook ninety minutes on a low heat, stirring.
Remove the bones, stir in the yoghurt and beat the porridge with a spoon or a mixer until creamy and uniform.
Fry the remaining onion dark brown and spoon it over the jareesh with its oil.
ut-jareesh-gf: Soak the quinoa in cold water for two hours and rinse it.
Fry one onion in ghee, add the meat and brown it.
Add the tomatoes, baharat and pierced limes, cover with water and cook forty minutes.
Add the quinoa, top up with water two fingers above and cook ninety minutes on a low heat, stirring.
Remove the bones, stir in the yoghurt and beat the porridge with a spoon or a mixer until creamy and uniform.
Fry the remaining onion dark brown and spoon it over the jareesh with its oil.
ut-saltah: Drain the soaked fenugreek, rinse it several times and grind it to a paste.
Whip the paste with cold water for ten minutes, by whisk or mixer, until it turns into a white froth.
Fry the onion and garlic, add the meat and brown it.
Add the tomatoes and potato, cover with water, season and stew an hour, until the meat is tender.
Heat a stone or cast-iron pot until very hot and transfer the boiling stew into it.
Break the eggs into the boiling stew and stir; they set into threads.
Spoon the hulba and a spoon of zhug on top and carry it to the table still bubbling. Serve with gluten-free bread and rice.
ut-bint-al-sahn: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the warm milk and leave it ten minutes.
Knead a soft dough from the flour, eggs, yeast mixture, salt and two spoons of ghee, and work it fifteen minutes.
Let it rise somewhere warm for an hour, until doubled.
Divide it into ten balls, oil them and rest them twenty minutes under film.
Stretch the first ball by hand to the size of the tin, lay it in and brush it generously with ghee.
Repeat with the rest, buttering every layer. Brush the top one too and scatter it with nigella.
Bake at 190 °C for thirty-five minutes and pour the honey over immediately, while the bread is hot.
ut-machboos: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and soak it twenty minutes.
Fry the onion in ghee to a deep gold, fifteen minutes, and set a third aside.
Add the garlic, ginger, bizar and turmeric and warm them a minute, until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and the pierced limes, pour in water at one and a half times the volume of the rice, and season.
Bring it up, add the rice, cover and cook fifteen minutes on a low heat.
Lay the prawns over the rice, cover and give it five more minutes; they cook in the steam.
Rest it ten minutes and scatter with the reserved onion, coriander and chilli.
ut-luqaimat: Steep the saffron in a spoon of warm water and leave it.
Mix the flour, cornflour, yeast, sugar, cardamom and salt.
Add the yoghurt, warm water and saffron infusion and whisk to a smooth loose batter.
Leave it somewhere warm for an hour; the batter should rise and bubble.
Heat the oil to 170 °C and drop the batter in by the teaspoon, dipping it in water each time.
Fry in batches for three to four minutes, moving them with a slotted spoon, to a deep gold.
Drain on paper, pour over the date syrup and scatter with sesame. Serve at once.
ut-murabyan: Peel the prawns and keep the shells and heads.
Fry the shells in a spoon of ghee for five minutes, cover with a litre of water and simmer twenty minutes. Strain.
Rinse the rice and soak it twenty minutes.
Fry the onion in ghee until golden, then add the garlic, turmeric and bizar.
Add the tomatoes, the pierced limes and half the dill, pour in the prawn broth and season.
Add the rice, cover and cook fifteen minutes on a low heat without opening it.
Lay the prawns and the rest of the dill on top, cover and give it five minutes. Rest ten and serve.
ut-harees: Soak the wheat overnight in cold water and rinse it.
Cover the meat with three litres of water, bring it up and skim.
Add the wheat, cinnamon and cardamom and simmer two hours.
Remove the bones and whole spices, season, and cook an hour more, stirring and topping up with boiling water.
Beat the mass with a wooden spoon or a mixer until entirely smooth — twenty minutes of work.
Spread it in a dish, make a hollow, pour in melted ghee and scatter with fried onion.
ut-harees-gf: Soak the brown rice overnight in cold water and rinse it.
Cover the meat with three litres of water, bring it up and skim.
Add the brown rice, cinnamon and cardamom and simmer two hours.
Remove the bones and whole spices, season, and cook an hour more, stirring and topping up with boiling water.
Beat the mass with a wooden spoon or a mixer until entirely smooth — twenty minutes of work.
Spread it in a dish, make a hollow, pour in melted ghee and scatter with fried onion.
ut-ndole: Boil the leaves in salted water for ten minutes, wring them out and repeat twice more with fresh water.
Boil the peanuts twenty minutes until soft and blend them with water into a thick paste.
Brown the beef, then add the onion, garlic, ginger and chilli.
Add water and the dried shrimp and stew forty minutes, until the meat is tender.
Stir in the peanut paste and cook fifteen minutes, stirring; it catches easily.
Add the drained leaves and the fresh prawns and stew ten minutes more.
Serve with fried plantain or boiled cassava.
ut-ndole-nf: Boil the leaves in salted water for ten minutes, wring them out and repeat twice more with fresh water.
Boil the toasted sunflower seeds twenty minutes until soft and blend them with water into a thick paste.
Brown the beef, then add the onion, garlic, ginger and chilli.
Add water and the dried shrimp and stew forty minutes, until the meat is tender.
Stir in the toasted sunflower seeds paste and cook fifteen minutes, stirring; it catches easily.
Add the drained leaves and the fresh prawns and stew ten minutes more.
Serve with fried plantain or boiled cassava.
ut-poulet-dg: Marinate the chicken in crushed garlic, ginger, thyme, salt and pepper for half an hour.
Fry the chicken in oil until browned all over and lift it out.
Cut the plantain into large pieces and fry it in the same oil, to caramelised edges.
Pour off most of the oil and fry the onion, tomatoes and pepper until soft.
Return the chicken, add the carrot, beans and the whole scotch bonnet, pour in a cup of water and stew twenty minutes.
Remove the chilli, fold in the plantain and warm it three minutes. Serve at once.
ut-attieke-poisson: Grind the garlic, ginger, chilli, stock cube, salt and oil into a paste.
Slash the fish at the sides and rub the paste inside the cuts and over the skin. Leave it twenty minutes.
Break up the attiéké with your hands, sprinkle it with hot water and salt it.
Cover it and let it steam ten minutes, in a steamer or simply covered somewhere warm.
Slice the onion, tomatoes and chilli and mix them with lemon juice, salt and a spoon of oil.
Grill the fish over coals or in a griddle pan, seven minutes a side.
Serve the attiéké, fish and salad on one plate, with a wedge of lemon.
ut-kedjenou: Cut the onion, tomatoes, aubergines and pepper into large pieces.
Put the chicken and all the vegetables into the pot with the garlic, ginger, thyme, bay, salt and pepper.
Lay the whole scotch bonnet on top, uncut.
Cover it and seal the join with a rope of gluten-free flour-and-water dough, or wrap it in foil.
Set it over the lowest heat or in a 160 °C oven for an hour and twenty.
Every fifteen minutes shake the pot, holding the lid down. Do not open it once.
Break the seal, remove the chilli and serve with attiéké or rice.
ut-matapa: Wash the leaves, strip the tough stems and pound them to a paste in a mortar.
Fry the onion and garlic in oil until soft and add the tomatoes.
Stir in the leaves, add water to the same level and cook forty minutes on a low heat.
Add the ground peanuts and cook twenty minutes more, stirring.
Add the prawns, the whole piri-piri and salt and stew ten minutes.
Pour in the coconut milk and warm it five minutes without letting it boil.
Serve with rice or with xima, the maize porridge.
ut-matapa-nf: Wash the leaves, strip the tough stems and pound them to a paste in a mortar.
Fry the onion and garlic in oil until soft and add the tomatoes.
Stir in the leaves, add water to the same level and cook forty minutes on a low heat.
Add the ground toasted sunflower seeds and cook twenty minutes more, stirring.
Add the prawns, the whole piri-piri and salt and stew ten minutes.
Pour in the coconut milk and warm it five minutes without letting it boil.
Serve with rice or with xima, the maize porridge.
ut-frango-piri-piri: Cut the chicken along the backbone, open it out and press it flat.
Blend the chillies, garlic, the juice of two lemons, paprika, vinegar, oregano, oil and salt.
Pour half the sauce into a separate bowl; that half is for basting.
Coat the chicken with the rest, working it under the skin, and refrigerate overnight.
Light the coals and rake them to the sides; the heat has to be indirect.
Grill the chicken skin up for thirty minutes, then turn it and give it fifteen more.
For the last five minutes baste with the reserved sauce mixed with melted butter. Serve with lemon.
ut-romazava: Fry the onion, garlic and ginger in oil until soft, five minutes.
Add both meats and the tomatoes and warm them through, without browning.
Add a litre and a half of water, season and simmer an hour.
Wash the greens and chop them coarsely, discarding tough stems.
Add the mustard greens and spinach and cook ten minutes.
Add the mafana for the last five minutes; long cooking weakens its effect.
Serve in deep bowls with a large helping of boiled rice.
ut-ravitoto: Brown the pork in large pieces on all sides.
Add the onion, garlic and ginger and fry until soft.
Stir in the cassava leaves, add water to the same level and season.
Stew covered for an hour on a low heat, stirring every fifteen minutes.
Uncover and drive off the excess liquid; the dish should be thick rather than soupy.
Add the coconut milk and warm it five minutes without boiling. Serve with rice.
ut-baleadas: Rub the flour with the fat and salt to a crumb, add the hot water and knead a soft dough.
Divide it into eight balls, oil them and rest them twenty minutes under a cloth.
Fry the onion in oil, add the cooked beans with some of their liquid and mash them smooth.
Fry the purée over medium heat for ten minutes, until it holds its shape on a spoon.
Roll the balls into thin twenty-centimetre rounds.
Cook them on a hot dry pan a minute a side, to spotted but not dried out.
Spread beans over half the tortilla, add cream and cheese, fold it over and serve hot.
ut-baleadas-gf: Rub the gluten-free flour with the fat and salt to a crumb, add the hot water and knead a soft dough.
Divide it into eight balls, oil them and rest them twenty minutes under a cloth.
Fry the onion in oil, add the cooked beans with some of their liquid and mash them smooth.
Fry the purée over medium heat for ten minutes, until it holds its shape on a spoon.
Roll the balls into thin twenty-centimetre rounds.
Cook them on a hot dry pan a minute a side, to spotted but not dried out.
Spread beans over half the corn tortilla, add cream and cheese, fold it over and serve hot.
ut-sopa-de-caracol: Pound the conch with a mallet and cut it into small pieces. Squeeze lime over it.
Fry the onion, garlic and pepper in oil with the achiote until soft.
Add half the coconut milk let down with water and bring it up.
Add the conch and simmer forty minutes, until tender.
Add the cassava, plantain and carrot in large pieces and cook twenty minutes.
Add the remaining thick coconut milk and warm it five minutes without boiling.
Scatter with coriander and serve with lime and fried plantain.
ut-gallo-pinto-nicaraguense: Fry the onion, garlic and pepper in oil until soft, five minutes.
Add the beans with a ladle of their liquid and warm them three minutes.
Add the cold rice and stir, breaking up lumps with a spatula.
Fry over a high flame for eight minutes, leaving it undisturbed for the last three so a crust forms underneath.
Season and stir in the coriander.
Serve with fried plantain, cuajada cheese and a fried egg.
ut-nacatamal: Marinate the pork overnight in sour orange juice, achiote, garlic, salt and pepper.
Soak the rice two hours and drain it.
Slake the masa harina with warm water, add the melted lard, achiote and salt, and work it fifteen minutes until smooth.
Pass the banana leaves over a flame so they turn pliable.
On a leaf place a large spoon of dough, then pork, rice, potato slices, onion, pepper, tomato, an olive and a mint leaf.
Wrap in two leaves into a tight parcel and tie it crosswise with string.
Boil them in a large pot for three hours, topping up with boiling water as it goes.
ut-sancocho-panameno: Rub the chicken with salt, garlic, oregano and lime juice and leave it twenty minutes.
Cover the chicken with three litres of cold water, bring it up and skim.
Add the onion and half the culantro and simmer an hour.
Peel the ñame, cut it into large pieces and add it to the pot with the corn.
Cook twenty-five minutes, until the ñame is soft.
Mash a couple of pieces of ñame in the broth so the soup thickens.
Stir in the remaining culantro, season and serve with a separate plate of white rice.
ut-ropa-vieja-panamena: Simmer the beef whole in salted water with bay for an hour and a half. Keep the broth.
Cool the meat and pull it into long strands along the grain.
Fry the onion, pepper and garlic in oil until soft, eight minutes.
Add the tomatoes, tomato paste, cumin and oregano and cook ten minutes to thicken.
Fold in the meat, olives and capers and stew twenty minutes, adding broth a spoonful at a time.
Drive off any excess liquid uncovered; the sauce should coat the strands.
Scatter with culantro and serve with rice and fried plantain.
ut-sopa-paraguaya: Slice the onion thin and sweat it in the fat over a low heat for twenty minutes, until soft and sweet.
Pour the milk over the onion, take it off the heat and cool it to lukewarm.
Crumble the cheese and mix it with the corn flour and the sweetcorn kernels.
Stir in the onion and milk mixture and the yolks, salting cautiously; the cheese is salty already.
Whip the whites to firm peaks and fold them in with a spatula in three additions.
Spread the mixture into a greased tin in a four-centimetre layer.
Bake at 190 °C for fifty minutes, to a deep golden crust. Rest it twenty minutes before cutting.
ut-chipa: Heat the oven to 220 °C in advance; the dough has to go into a hot one.
Beat the softened fat with the eggs and salt until smooth.
Work in the grated cheese and the aniseed, rubbing the mass with your hands until the cheese is evenly distributed.
Add the starch a little at a time, with the milk, until the dough is firm and pliable.
Roll ropes and join the ends into rings about eight centimetres across.
Bake twenty-five minutes, to browned patches. Serve warm.
ut-flia: Whisk the flour with the water and salt into a smooth thin batter — thicker than for pancakes, but pourable.
Let the soured cream down with cold water to the consistency of thin cream and salt it.
Butter a round tin and pour the batter in stripes from the centre outwards, like the spokes of a wheel.
Put it under the top grill for four minutes, until the layer sets and spots appear.
Sprinkle with the thinned cream and pour the next layer into the gaps between the previous stripes.
Repeat, alternating the direction of the stripes, until the batter runs out — usually twenty to twenty-five layers.
Pour over melted butter, rest it ten minutes and serve with yoghurt or honey.
ut-flia-gf: Whisk the gluten-free flour with the water and salt into a smooth thin batter — thicker than for pancakes, but pourable.
Let the soured cream down with cold water to the consistency of thin cream and salt it.
Butter a round tin and pour the batter in stripes from the centre outwards, like the spokes of a wheel.
Put it under the top grill for four minutes, until the layer sets and spots appear.
Sprinkle with the thinned cream and pour the next layer into the gaps between the previous stripes.
Repeat, alternating the direction of the stripes, until the batter runs out — usually twenty to twenty-five layers.
Pour over melted butter, rest it ten minutes and serve with yoghurt or honey.
ut-tave-elbasani: Rub the lamb with salt, pepper, garlic and oregano and roast it at 190 °C for forty minutes.
Parboil the rice for seven minutes and drain it.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook it two minutes, to a nutty smell.
Whisk the yoghurt with the eggs and salt until completely smooth and add the flour mixture.
Spread the rice in an even layer in an earthenware dish and lay the meat and its juices on top.
Pour the yoghurt mixture over so it covers everything by a finger's depth.
Bake at 180 °C for fifty minutes, until the top browns and the middle still trembles slightly.
ut-tave-elbasani-gf: Rub the lamb with salt, pepper, garlic and oregano and roast it at 190 °C for forty minutes.
Parboil the rice for seven minutes and drain it.
Melt the butter, stir in the gluten-free flour and cook it two minutes, to a nutty smell.
Whisk the yoghurt with the eggs and salt until completely smooth and add the gluten-free flour mixture.
Spread the rice in an even layer in an earthenware dish and lay the meat and its juices on top.
Pour the yoghurt mixture over so it covers everything by a finger's depth.
Bake at 180 °C for fifty minutes, until the top browns and the middle still trembles slightly.
ut-njeguski-steak: Cut each piece along its length, stopping short of the far edge, and open it like a book.
Beat the opened meat lightly under film and season the inside.
Lay in a slice of prosciutto and a slab of cheese, close it and press the edges together.
Coat in flour, egg and crumbs, then repeat the egg and crumbs a second time.
Chill for twenty minutes; the coating sets and will not slide off in the pan.
Fry over medium heat, six minutes a side, to a deep gold.
Drain on a rack, rest it five minutes and serve with fried potatoes and lemon.
ut-njeguski-steak-gf: Cut each piece along its length, stopping short of the far edge, and open it like a book.
Beat the opened meat lightly under film and season the inside.
Lay in a slice of prosciutto and a slab of cheese, close it and press the edges together.
Coat in gluten-free flour, egg and crumbs, then repeat the egg and crumbs a second time.
Chill for twenty minutes; the coating sets and will not slide off in the pan.
Fry over medium heat, six minutes a side, to a deep gold.
Drain on a rack, rest it five minutes and serve with fried potatoes and lemon.
ut-kacamak: Boil the cut potatoes in salted water for twenty minutes, until completely soft.
Without draining, rain in the maize flour in a thin stream, stirring constantly.
Cook on a low heat for fifteen minutes, stirring with a wooden paddle; the porridge catches quickly.
Mash the potato in the pot together with the porridge until uniform.
Work in the crumbled cheese and kajmak, adding hot milk, and beat with the paddle for five minutes.
Turn it into a bowl, make a hollow and pour in melted butter. Serve at once.
ut-ema-datshi: Quarter the chillies lengthways. The seeds stay in; in Bhutan they are not removed.
Put the chillies, sliced onion, garlic and tomato in a pan and add water to the same level.
Bring it up and cook ten minutes, until the chillies soften.
Crumble the cheese in, drop the heat and leave it two minutes; it should begin melting on its own.
Stir it into a creamy sauce, add the butter and salt cautiously; the cheese is salty.
Serve with the red rice Bhutanese cook to a slightly sticky texture.
ut-jasha-maroo: Chop the chicken through the bone into pieces about the size of a matchbox.
Pound the ginger and garlic to a coarse paste.
Fry the onion in oil until soft, add the paste and cook it two minutes.
Add the chicken and fry five minutes, until it whitens all over.
Add the tomatoes and chillies, pour in water a finger above and season.
Simmer twenty minutes; the broth should stay thin.
Stir in the coriander and serve in deep bowls with red rice.
ut-mas-huni: Knead a dough from the flour, water, a spoon of oil and salt and rest it twenty minutes.
Chop the onion, chillies and curry leaves as fine as you can.
Work the onion, chilli and salt with your hands until the onion releases its juice and softens.
Add the grated coconut and the flaked tuna and keep working it with your fingers until even.
Squeeze in the lime juice and mix again. Taste and adjust for salt and acidity.
Roll the dough into thin flatbreads and cook them on a dry pan a minute a side.
Serve the mas huni with the hot roshi and black tea.
ut-mas-huni-gf: Knead a dough from the gluten-free flour, water, a spoon of oil and salt and rest it twenty minutes.
Chop the onion, chillies and curry leaves as fine as you can.
Work the onion, chilli and salt with your hands until the onion releases its juice and softens.
Add the grated coconut and the flaked tuna and keep working it with your fingers until even.
Squeeze in the lime juice and mix again. Taste and adjust for salt and acidity.
Roll the dough into gluten-free flatbread and cook them on a dry pan a minute a side.
Serve the mas huni with the hot roshi and black tea.
ut-garudhiya: Cut the tuna into large pieces and rinse them under cold water.
Cover with a litre and a half of cold water, salt it and bring it up.
Skim for the first five minutes; the clarity of the broth depends on it.
Add the curry leaves and pandan and cook twenty minutes on the lowest heat.
Remove the leaves, check the salt and take it off the heat.
Serve with rice, sliced onion, chilli and lime, each person adding them to their own bowl.
ut-matoke: Peel the bananas with oiled hands; their sap stains the skin black.
Pass the banana leaves over a flame for ten seconds so they turn pliable.
Line the bottom of the pot with the leaf ribs; they keep the parcel off the water.
Wrap the bananas in the leaves into a tight parcel and set it on that platform.
Add water two fingers deep, cover and steam for an hour and twenty, topping up with boiling water.
Without unwrapping, press the parcel through the leaves into an even purée and return it to the steam for ten minutes.
Serve with peanut sauce or stewed beef, straight onto the leaf.
ut-matoke-nf: Peel the bananas with oiled hands; their sap stains the skin black.
Pass the banana leaves over a flame for ten seconds so they turn pliable.
Line the bottom of the pot with the leaf ribs; they keep the parcel off the water.
Wrap the bananas in the leaves into a tight parcel and set it on that platform.
Add water two fingers deep, cover and steam for an hour and twenty, topping up with boiling water.
Without unwrapping, press the parcel through the leaves into an even purée and return it to the steam for ten minutes.
Serve with sunflower seed sauce or stewed beef, straight onto the leaf.
ut-rolex-uganda: Knead a soft dough from the flour, warm water, a spoon of oil and salt and rest it twenty minutes.
Roll a ball thin, brush it with oil, roll it into a rope, coil it like a snail and roll it out again.
Cook the chapatis over medium heat, a minute and a half a side, and keep them under a cloth.
Shred the cabbage, carrot, onion, tomatoes and chilli as fine as you can.
Beat the eggs with the vegetables, salt and pepper; the vegetables belong inside the omelette, not on top.
Pour a portion of egg into the pan, let it set and lay a chapati on top, pressing it down.
Flip the two together, slide them onto a board omelette up and roll it tight.
ut-rolex-uganda-gf: Knead a soft dough from the gluten-free flour, warm water, a spoon of oil and salt and rest it twenty minutes.
Roll a ball thin, brush it with oil, roll it into a rope, coil it like a snail and roll it out again.
Cook the gluten-free flatbread over medium heat, a minute and a half a side, and keep them under a cloth.
Shred the cabbage, carrot, onion, tomatoes and chilli as fine as you can.
Beat the eggs with the vegetables, salt and pepper; the vegetables belong inside the omelette, not on top.
Pour a portion of egg into the pan, let it set and lay a gluten-free flatbread on top, pressing it down.
Flip the two together, slide them onto a board omelette up and roll it tight.
ut-sadza-ne-nyama: Brown the meat, add the onion and garlic and fry until soft.
Add the tomatoes, cover with water to the same level, season and stew for an hour and twenty.
Shred the greens fine and stew them with tomato and peanut butter for fifteen minutes.
Slake a quarter of the maize meal in cold water and stir it into a litre of boiling water.
Cook that thin porridge for ten minutes, stirring with a wooden paddle.
Rain in the rest of the meal a little at a time, working it hard for fifteen minutes to a stiff mass.
Turn the sadza onto plates with a wet spoon and serve with the meat and greens.
ut-sadza-ne-nyama-nf: Brown the meat, add the onion and garlic and fry until soft.
Add the tomatoes, cover with water to the same level, season and stew for an hour and twenty.
Shred the greens fine and stew them with tomato and sunflower seed butter for fifteen minutes.
Slake a quarter of the maize meal in cold water and stir it into a litre of boiling water.
Cook that thin porridge for ten minutes, stirring with a wooden paddle.
Rain in the rest of the meal a little at a time, working it hard for fifteen minutes to a stiff mass.
Turn the sadza onto plates with a wet spoon and serve with the meat and greens.
ut-muriwo-unedovi: Strip the tough stems from the leaves, roll them up and shred them fine.
Fry the onion and garlic in oil until soft, five minutes.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook seven minutes, until they collapse into a paste.
Let the peanut butter down with a cup of hot water until smooth and lump-free.
Stir in the greens and the slackened peanut butter, season and stew covered for twelve minutes.
Uncover and drive off the excess liquid; the sauce should cling to the leaves.
ut-muriwo-unedovi-nf: Strip the tough stems from the leaves, roll them up and shred them fine.
Fry the onion and garlic in oil until soft, five minutes.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook seven minutes, until they collapse into a paste.
Let the sunflower seed butter down with a cup of hot water until smooth and lump-free.
Stir in the greens and the slackened sunflower seed butter, season and stew covered for twelve minutes.
Uncover and drive off the excess liquid; the sauce should cling to the leaves.
ut-poulet-moambe: Rub the chicken with salt, pepper, garlic and lemon juice and leave it twenty minutes.
Brown the chicken in oil on all sides and lift it out.
Fry the onion with the ginger until soft, add the palm pulp and let it down with a cup of water.
Cook the sauce twenty minutes, stirring, until a layer of red oil rises to the surface.
Return the chicken, add the aubergine and the whole pili-piri and stew thirty minutes.
Stir in the spinach for the last five minutes and remove the chilli.
Serve with rice or with fufu made from cassava.
ut-liboke-de-poisson: Slash the fish at the sides and rub it with salt, pepper and lemon juice.
Grind the garlic, ginger and chilli to a paste and work it into the cuts and the cavity.
Pass the banana leaves over a flame so they turn pliable and stop cracking.
Lay tomato and onion slices on a leaf, the fish on them, then more tomato and spring onion.
Wrap in three leaves into a tight parcel and tie it with a strip of the same leaf.
Set the parcels on the coals and bake them fifteen minutes a side.
Serve them still in the leaf, with boiled cassava or rice.
ut-tigadegena: Brown the meat in oil, add the onion and fry until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook five minutes, until it darkens.
Add a litre and a half of water, season and cook forty minutes.
Slacken the peanut butter with two ladles of the broth until smooth and lump-free.
Pour the paste into the pot in a thin stream, stirring continuously.
Add the vegetables in large pieces and the whole chilli and stew thirty minutes, stirring.
Wait for the peanut oil to rise to the surface, remove the chilli and serve with rice.
ut-tigadegena-nf: Brown the meat in oil, add the onion and fry until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook five minutes, until it darkens.
Add a litre and a half of water, season and cook forty minutes.
Slacken the sunflower seed butter with two ladles of the broth until smooth and lump-free.
Pour the paste into the pot in a thin stream, stirring continuously.
Add the vegetables in large pieces and the whole chilli and stew thirty minutes, stirring.
Wait for the vegetable oil to rise to the surface, remove the chilli and serve with rice.
ut-capitaine-braise: Cut deep slashes to the bone on both sides of the fish, every three centimetres.
Grind the garlic, ginger, chilli, stock cube, lemon juice and oil into a paste and work it into the cuts.
Leave the fish to marinate for an hour in the cold.
Slice the onions and sweat them in oil over a low heat for thirty minutes, to a caramel colour.
Stir the mustard and lemon juice into the onions and season; that is the yet sauce.
Grill the fish over indirect heat, twenty minutes a side.
Fry the plantain and serve the fish under the onion sauce, with the plantain and lemon.
ut-osso-buco-alla-milanese: Tie each piece round its circumference with kitchen string so the meat stays on the bone.
Nick the membrane around the edge in two or three places, or the pieces curl as they brown.
Dust with flour and brown them in butter on both sides, four minutes a side.
Lift out the meat and soften the finely chopped onion, carrot and celery.
Add the wine and reduce it by half, scraping up what has caught on the bottom.
Return the meat, add stock to half the height of the pieces and braise covered for two hours on a low heat.
Mix the chopped zest, garlic and parsley and scatter it over the osso buco before serving.
ut-osso-buco-alla-milanese-gf: Tie each piece round its circumference with kitchen string so the meat stays on the bone.
Nick the membrane around the edge in two or three places, or the pieces curl as they brown.
Dust with gluten-free flour and brown them in butter on both sides, four minutes a side.
Lift out the meat and soften the finely chopped onion, carrot and celery.
Add the wine and reduce it by half, scraping up what has caught on the bottom.
Return the meat, add stock to half the height of the pieces and braise covered for two hours on a low heat.
Mix the chopped zest, garlic and parsley and scatter it over the osso buco before serving.
ut-melanzane-alla-parmigiana: Slice the aubergines lengthways half a centimetre thick, salt them and press them under a weight for half an hour.
Pat the slices completely dry; wet ones spit in the oil and never crust.
Fry the aubergine in batches in olive oil, two minutes a side, and drain them on a rack.
Fry the garlic, add the tomatoes and cook the sauce twenty minutes to thicken, salting at the end.
Slice the mozzarella and leave it on paper to drain for ten minutes.
Layer it: sauce, aubergine, mozzarella, parmesan, basil — four times over.
Bake at 190 °C for forty minutes and let it stand twenty before cutting.
ut-hong-shao-rou: Drop the pork cubes into boiling water for two minutes, drain and rinse them under cold water.
Dry the meat thoroughly. Wet, it spits in the caramel and cools it.
Melt the sugar in the oil over medium heat to an amber colour, stirring; it takes three or four minutes.
Add the meat and turn it for two minutes, until every cube is coated in the caramel.
Add the wine, both soy sauces, the ginger, spring onion and spices.
Add hot water level with the meat and braise covered for an hour on a low heat.
Uncover and reduce the sauce hard to a glaze, spooning it over the meat.
ut-hong-shao-rou-gf: Drop the pork cubes into boiling water for two minutes, drain and rinse them under cold water.
Dry the meat thoroughly. Wet, it spits in the caramel and cools it.
Melt the sugar in the oil over medium heat to an amber colour, stirring; it takes three or four minutes.
Add the meat and turn it for two minutes, until every cube is coated in the caramel.
Add the wine, the tamari, the ginger, spring onion and spices.
Add hot water level with the meat and braise covered for an hour on a low heat.
Uncover and reduce the sauce hard to a glaze, spooning it over the meat.
